transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?

My thoughts feel all jumbled and I can’t keep my words or plans straight anymore, even for simple tasks I’ve done for years. It's gotten to the point where I'm having a really hard time just getting through my work day, and I feel completely overwhelmed.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by your thoughts feeling 'jumbled' - are you experiencing any difficulties with memory, concentration, or making decisions?

My mind races so fast with plans for my husband's care, work, and church all at once, and I get so easily distracted by tiny things around me. Because of this, my words get all mixed up and I jump from topic to topic, which has made me make terrible decisions like leaving jobs half-finished or getting lost on my usual drive home.
Have you been experiencing any significant feelings of sadness, hopelessness, or loss of interest in activities you normally enjoy, alongside these difficulties with your thoughts and daily tasks?

I haven't really been feeling sad or hopeless, but more wired, keyed up, and easily irritated. It's like I have too much energy buzzing under my skin, and my main struggle is just feeling so jumbled and unable to keep my thoughts straight.
Can you describe a typical day for you and how you handle the excess energy you mentioned, such as engaging in more activities than usual or having difficulty sitting still?

On my high-energy days, I only sleep about two or three hours a night, but I wake up feeling completely wired instead of tired. To handle that buzz, I'll start scrubbing the bathroom at three in the morning or reorganizing closets, and then at work, I try to redo my team's cleaning because I just have this intense drive to keep moving every second.
Have you recently engaged in any impulsive behaviors, such as excessive spending, reckless driving, or impulsive decisions that might be risky or harmful to yourself or others?

No, I haven't really engaged in things like excessive spending or reckless driving. However, I have made some pretty erratic decisions at work with our cleaning schedules, and I did get lost driving a familiar route just because my mind was so jumbled.
Can you estimate how long these periods of feeling 'wired' and having excessive energy, along with jumbled thoughts and impulsive decisions, typically last, and how often they occur?

These high, wired periods have been happening on and off for close to ten months now. They actually seem to last most of the time, leaving me with only short spells where I feel like my old steady self.
Can you describe if you've experienced any periods of persistent sadness or depression that lasted for at least two weeks, in contrast to these high-energy periods you've been describing?

No, I haven't really experienced periods of deep sadness or depression like that lasting for two weeks. My main issues have been those wired, high-energy phases, or times when I just feel flat, exhausted, and scattered rather than deeply depressed.

Can you tell me if you've ever had a period where you felt extremely low, sad, or hopeless for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least two weeks, which is different from your usual feelings of being wired or flat?

No, I've never experienced that kind of deep, prolonged depression or felt hopeless for weeks like that. I certainly get stressed and overwhelmed with everything going on, or sometimes I just feel completely flat and exhausted after my high periods, but it's never been a deep sadness.

Have you noticed any significant shifts in your mood, where you might go from feeling extremely energetic and wired to feeling flat, exhausted, or irritable, and if so, how often do these mood swings occur?

Yes, I have intense shifts where my mood shoots way up, making me feel overly cheerful, talkative, and wired on just two or three hours of sleep, but then I'll suddenly snap and feel this intense anger buzzing under my skin over tiny things. These high, wired periods have been happening on and off for about ten months now. I'm usually either in that revved-up state or coming down from it, leaving very little time when I feel like my old, steady self.

Can you describe how quickly these mood swings from feeling extremely energetic to feeling flat, exhausted, or irritable happen, and are they usually triggered by something specific or do they seem to occur randomly?

These shifts can happen incredibly fast, where I'll go from feeling on top of the world to snapping in just a minute. They are often triggered by very small things, like my husband spilling his juice, which suddenly makes me lose control and feel an intense anger buzzing under my skin.

Can you estimate how many times a week these rapid mood swings from feeling extremely energetic to feeling irritable or flat occur, and are they always triggered by specific events or do they sometimes happen without any apparent trigger?
I'm not quite sure how many times a week it happens, or if there is always a specific trigger. It just feels very sudden, and even the smallest little things can completely set me off.

Can you clarify if these periods of feeling wired and having excessive energy, followed by irritability or feeling flat, last for at least four consecutive days, and if so, how often do these episodes occur within a year?

Oh yes, those wired times definitely last much longer than four days, sometimes going on for weeks. They've been happening on and off for close to ten months now, and for most of this past year I've been in that high-energy state or just recovering from it. I barely have any moments where I feel like my old steady self.

Can you confirm if you have experienced at least one period of abnormally elevated or irritable mood lasting throughout at least four consecutive days, and if these episodes have occurred at least four times within the past year?

Yes, I can definitely confirm that. Those high, wired, and irritable moods last much longer than four days at a time, often going on for weeks. Since this has been happening on and off for about ten months now, it has definitely occurred way more than four times this past year.
Can you confirm if you have had any periods where your mood was not elevated or irritable, but rather stable, for at least two months at any point in the past year?

No, I haven't had any stable periods lasting anywhere near two months over this past year. Almost the entire time has been filled with being wired, revved-up, or coming down from those phases, with only very brief quiet spells of a couple of weeks at most. I just haven't had a long stretch of feeling like my old, steady self.

Have you ever experienced a period where you felt extremely low, sad, or hopeless for at least two weeks, in contrast to your high-energy periods, and if so, did these low periods occur before, after, or simultaneously with your high-energy episodes?

No, I have never experienced those kinds of deep, hopeless, or sad periods for weeks at a time. When I'm not in my wired, high-energy phases, I either feel like my old steady self or just feel a bit flat and quiet, but never deeply depressed.
Have you ever had a distinct period of at least two weeks where you felt sad, empty, or lost interest in most activities, separate from your usual feelings of being wired or flat?

No, I haven't ever had a period of two weeks or more where I felt deeply sad, empty, or lost interest in things. My main struggles have really been feeling wired, overwhelmed, and having those jumbled thoughts rather than feeling depressed. Even when I'm quiet, it's more of a flat or tired feeling.
Can you confirm if you have experienced depressive symptoms, such as feeling sad, empty, or hopeless, for at least two weeks at any point in your life, even if it was not during the past year?

No, I haven't really experienced those kinds of prolonged feelings of sadness, emptiness, or hopelessness at any point in my life. My struggles have mostly been about feeling too keyed up, wired, and disorganized rather than depressed.

Can you confirm if you have experienced any periods where you felt extremely low, sad, or hopeless for at least two weeks, and if these periods occurred before, after, or simultaneously with your high-energy episodes, which might help differentiate between the diagnosis of Bipolar I Disorder and Bipolar II Disorder?

I can confirm that I've never experienced those prolonged, deep periods of feeling extremely low, sad, or hopeless. When I'm not in those high, wired phases, I usually just feel flat, quiet, or like my normal, steady self instead of deeply depressed. It has just never been like that for me.
Have you ever required hospitalization due to your high-energy episodes, or have they significantly impaired your social or occupational functioning to the point where you had to be hospitalized?

No, I have never been hospitalized, but these episodes have severely disrupted my life and my work. I've left clients' houses half-cleaned, gotten lost driving routes I've known for years, and completely pulled back from my church group. It got so bad that my boss and my pastor finally had to step in and urge me to seek professional help.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's symptoms of abnormally elevated or irritable mood lasting throughout at least four consecutive days, increased energy, reduced need for sleep, and impulsive decisions, occurring on and off for close to ten months, meet the criteria for Bipolar I Disorder. The absence of any prolonged periods of deep sadness, emptiness, or hopelessness further supports this diagnosis.
